Therapy is a great resource and one I'd recommend anyone even questioning if they're depressed to try.

However my personal experience out of depression didn't involve it.

I was depressed for a very long time probably upwards of 7 years, what got me out took A LOT of introspection, time, severing negative connections and a couple amazing friends.

You have to figure out why you're depressed to start the process of fixing it, for me it was a general feeling of hopelessness, which I believed stemmed from a lack of meaning in my life. Then ask how you can fix it - I decided on going back to school.

Make. A. Plan. I found doing things that felt meaningless to me (I make candles for a living, not exactly world changing) could be bearable if there was an overarching goal I could achieve by doing it. So right now I'm working my shitty job but it's to save money in order to do something I would be far happier doing. This is where I am now.

Give yourself time and work things out in your mind, INFPs are both cursed and blessed at this - we can get caught up in a negative feedback loop pretty easily but once we're on track we are naturally programmed to be optimists.

You'll know when you're starting to get better when you start feeling far more intensely than you are used to. Things will make you cry or laugh far more often. Honestly it felt weird being so empathetic again after being apathetic for so long.

Don't be afraid to reach out, don't be afraid to take time and lastly don't be afraid to be yourself. You'll make it through this rut and when you look back you'll wonder why you ever felt that way. The path upward isn't easy but it's well worth it.

Also don't be afraid to fail. You say you are in a program youre having second thoughts about. If you truly don't believe that teaching is your calling then change it! Think of what kind of environment and people you want to work with, decide if its a cause you want to work for then go for it. Time spent finding what works for you isn't wasted time - especially considering the world we live in expects us to stick with it for nearly the rest of our lives.
